# Specialized metadata-hashing manifests

Only Cargo.toml files are adapted. Every staged src/**/*.rs file, generic-array/build.rs, license and README is byte-identical to the recorded upstream Git blob. Cargo.toml.upstream preserves each original manifest. SOURCE-PROVENANCE.json records per-file immutable URLs, Git SHA-1 identities, sizes and SHA-256 hashes; PINS.json records repositories and commits.

All dependencies use exact version + relative path. All registry-only optional/dev dependencies and unsupported optional features are removed; no [patch.crates-io], network registry fallback, source edits, dynamically loaded crypto library, build-time dependency download or hand-written SHA-256 adapter is involved. Package metadata and licenses remain upstream; publish=false prevents publishing specialized packages. Docs metadata referring to removed features is omitted.

- sha2: path-pin digest/cfg-if; omit the cpufeatures/sha2-asm architecture dependency table and dev dependencies; omit asm, asm-aarch64, loongarch64_asm and oid features. Default features now include force-soft as well as std; force-soft-compact and compress remain. BOTH SHA-256 and SHA-512 upstream dispatch modules test force-soft(-compact) before architecture branches, so selected software backends never reference cpufeatures/sha2-asm. Every caller must request force-soft or force-soft-compact when disabling defaults. A caller disabling defaults without either software feature is outside this specialized manifest's supported surface and can fail to compile on x86/x86_64; this is intentional fail-closed behavior, not architecture autodetection.
- digest: keep core-api/block-buffer, alloc and std; remove registry-only subtle, blobby, const-oid and unsupported mac/rand_core/oid/dev feature declarations. Complete upstream src remains present including those gated modules.
- crypto-common: path-pin generic-array (with upstream more_lengths) and typenum; keep std; omit rand_core/getrandom.
- block-buffer: only path-pin generic-array.
- generic-array: retain original build.rs, production source, more_lengths, and build dependency version_check; path-pin typenum/version_check. Remove optional serde/zeroize and dev dependencies, metadata/badges, and the packaging include list (it names omitted CHANGELOG). Its build.rs queries rustc --version using version_check and emits relaxed_coherence/deprecation/check-cfg settings; it does not download source.
- typenum: complete checked-in src including src/gen retained; remove optional scale-info and its feature; preserve other no-dependency features. Remove upstream generate workspace. Set build=false because upstream build.rs only generates upstream tests.rs; production src uses committed src/gen, not OUT_DIR. The test generator is deliberately absent from this production-only stage. No upstream test/example/CI directories staged.
- cfg-if: omit optional rustc-std-workspace-core and rustc-dep-of-std (irrelevant outside the Rust standard-library build).
- version_check: only specialize library path/publish metadata; no dependencies.

Removed optional feature names remain in upstream source cfgs. The first authorized product compile succeeded and reported these expected source/manifest mismatches. Active manifests now add exact [lints.rust] unexpected_cfgs check-cfg entries: sha2 asm/loongarch64_asm/oid; digest dev/mac/oid/rand_core; crypto-common rand_core; generic-array serde/zeroize and the build-script cfg relaxed_coherence; typenum scale_info. This recognizes unchanged source conditions without enabling a feature or exposing unsupported APIs. The lint stays at warn; unknown conditions outside these exact names still warn. No global warning suppression is used. Upstream deprecation/lifetime warnings remain visible.

Original staging ran no upstream code. Task 5 product integration authorizes offline lock generation and ordinary product compilation; its exact commands/logs/results are recorded in task-5-report.md. No tests, lint, benchmarks, executable probes or app/game/helper launches are authorized or performed. Source-byte hashing only identifies artifacts; compilation is not vector or performance qualification. All active manifest headers locate this shared record at ../metadata-sha256/MANIFEST-ADAPTATIONS.md.
